about: Product pictures and clips of Slick for the website and the README. The stills without a clip or still field were captured from the launcher's own interface code drawing a made-up sample catalog over a wallpaper generated in code, at 2x on a Retina display, by scripts/ui-showcase.sh. The clips, the entries with a clip field, are recordings of the assembled app running the storyboard that field names, by make media: real search, ranking, learning, features and glass, over the same wallpaper. They list Apple's own apps from /System/Applications with their real names and icons, and nothing from /Applications or the home folder. Opening an app is recorded instead of done. Copied text, files and other data in them are made up for the clip. The entries with a still field are pictures that a storyboard's still steps took during its clip: the real settings window, and the panel in the Spotlight and Glass themes. The Glass clips and the pair of Standard and Glass stills show the panel over the About page of the settings window, so clear glass has something to show through. Each clip has an MP4 for the website, a GIF for the README and a poster PNG.

Escape closes them, and Return pastes the color and the panel closes. Recorded from the assembled app running a scripted scenario, with Apple's own apps and their real icons. files.caption: The Spotlight theme puts the query in a capsule of glass and the results in a separate container below it.
files.alt: A recording of Slick's search panel in the Spotlight theme, dark mode, over a purple gradient wallpaper. The theme draws two pieces of glass. A tall capsule holds the search field and a glowing caret. Below it, apart from it, a rounded container holds the results. The panel opens with Music, Notes, Mail and Calendar suggested, each with its Command-digit shortcut at the right. Typing “c”, “a” and “l” narrows the results, and the field completes “calendar” in grey. With “cal” the container shows Calendar, Calculator, Calculator History, Quit All Applications and Eject All Disks. The selection moves down to Calculator. Command-K opens the action panel inside the results container, which grows to fit it. It lists Open, Show in Finder, Show Package Contents, Copy Name, Copy Bundle Identifier and Copy Path with their shortcuts, then Add to Favorites and Set Alias. Command-K closes it again. Return picks Calculator and the panel closes. The scenario notes the launch instead of opening the app. Recorded from the assembled app running a scripted scenario, with Apple's own apps and their real icons.
